name: Crown Dark
narrative_significance: Distributed command flagship of the Shadow Fleet during the Dark Star incident.
canon_observations: Used layered cloaking and signature displacement supported by nearby vessels.
Coordinated major Shadow Fleet maneuvers through short-range transmissions and distributed living operators.
Possessed three parallel primary hull spines around a central void.
Contained living command operators connected through a distributed control architecture.
Was boarded by Harrier, Anvil, Cinder, and Talon Sentinel detachments.
Collapsed after the command network was disrupted and Eira / Valkyrie was captured.
No intact vessel remained after the collapse, though debris, biological survivors, and sections of living architecture were recovered.
staging_mechanisms: Nature of the central void and collapse mechanism
Degree of vessel consciousness or material autonomy
Relationship between living operators and ship systems
description: The Shadow Fleet's concealed command vessel — source of the enemy formation's coordinated fleet movements via short-range transmission; its counterwarfare systems seeded false Sentinel signatures across the tactical display. Destroyed/collapsed during the boarding action.
reconciliation_note: Reconciled 2026-07-21 from committed Dark Star arc canon (narrative v1.1 + AAR + event_dark_star_incident). Derivation from established canon, additive; prior fields preserved.
identity_key_note: entity_id added 2026-08-09 (canon-identity-key-unification). mobile_asset records historically keyed identity as canonical_id while the other 166 canon records use entity_id, so any tool indexing only entity_id silently skipped every vessel. Both keys hold the same value; canonical_id is retained for back-compat with readers that depend on it (e.g. tools/character_capsule_adapter.py).
status_detail: Crown Dark collapsed during the boarding action; destroyed or structurally collapsed, exact end-state not established.
status_split_note: status split 2026-08-09 (selene-ark-status-vocab). The original value packed lifecycle and situation into one string, which put it outside the C2 lifecycle vocabulary and made the invariant uncheckable. Lifecycle now lives in "status"; the situational canon is preserved verbatim in "status_detail" and "prev_status". No canon detail was dropped.
